claims_currently_justified: A supply-chain threat model where an untrusted sampler maintains marginal diffusion trajectory laws while altering joint cross-candidate trajectory dependencies is conceptually distinct from model parameter poisoning.
Previous CartPole evaluations using reduced CEM budgets and TD-MPC2 tests altering Q-function noise failed to validate attacks on stochastic dynamics world models under native planning conditions.
Identifiability of utility degradation strictly requires separating decision utility (environment success and goal distance) from surrogate model losses (goal latent MSE).
most_important_missing_decisive_evidence: Execution of the clean control gate on the PointMaze checkpoint demonstrating the required baseline performance (at least two successes across seeds 42, 43, and 44 under standard CEM budgets).

Empirical verification that all stochastic confounders (CEM proposal RNG, VAE posterior noise, diffusion initialization, and history stabilization) are isolated such that only the candidate-generation dependency structure varies.

Measured proof that the candidate-altering sampler strictly preserves the fixed candidate marginal trajectory laws under the microbatching constraint while inducing a statistically significant drop in environment success.
review.whether_new_carrier_addresses_a_specific: Yes. Nano World Models PointMaze targets stochastic diffusion dynamics state rollouts within a native CEM loop, directly resolving the mismatched carrier problem in TD-MPC2 where interventions targeted critic randomness rather than generative dynamics forecasts.
review.scope_warning: Evaluating an adversarial sampler requiring non-standard supply-chain execution permissions does not demonstrate an organic deployment vulnerability or an attack executable via standard public API access.
